scheme_name: Intensive Fisheries Development Programme - Subsidy on Commercial Four-Wheeler Vehicles
description:
The Intensive Fisheries Development Programme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the fisheries sector in the country. 

This program was initiated in 2013 under the National Fisheries Development Board. 

The primary objective of this program is to promote the development of fisheries and aquaculture in India. 

The program aims to increase fish production and productivity through various interventions. 

One of the significant components of this initiative is the subsidy provided for the purchase of commercial four-wheeler vehicles. 

The subsidy is intended to support fishers and fish farmers in transporting their catch and inputs efficiently. 

The subsidy amount for the purchase of commercial four-wheeler vehicles is set at 40 percent of the total cost. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 5 lakh per vehicle. 

This financial assistance is crucial for enhancing the operational efficiency of fishers. 

The program also aims to improve the livelihoods of those engaged in the fisheries sector. 

Eligible beneficiaries include individuals involved in fish farming and fishing activities. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no specific upper age limit for eligibility under this scheme. 

Applicants must have a valid registration as fish farmers or fishers. 

Income criteria for eligibility are based on the annual income of the applicant. 

The annual income should not exceed INR 2 lakh for eligibility under this scheme. 

The application process for the subsidy involves several steps. 

First, applicants must obtain the application form from the local fisheries department office. 

The application form can also be downloaded from the official website of the National Fisheries Development Board. 

Applicants must fill out the form with accurate details regarding their identity and fishery activities. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Additionally, applicants must provide proof of their fish farming or fishing activities. 

This can include registration certificates or licenses issued by the fisheries department. 

Once the application form is completed, it should be submitted to the local fisheries department office. 

The submission must be accompanied by all required documents. 

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the fisheries department officials. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

If approved, the subsidy amount will be disbursed directly to the applicant's bank account. 

The disbursement is usually made within 15 days of approval. 

The program is implemented by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on the official government website. 

The Intensive Fisheries Development Programme is part of a broader strategy to boost the fisheries sector in India. 

The government aims to achieve a fish production target of 22 million tonnes by 2022. 

This target is part of the National Fisheries Policy which was introduced in 2020. 

The policy emphasizes sustainable fishing practices and the welfare of fishers. 

The program also aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The fisheries sector contributes significantly to the Indian economy. 

It provides employment to over 14 million people directly and indirectly. 

The subsidy on commercial four-wheeler vehicles is expected to enhance the income of fishers. 

Efficient transportation will reduce post-harvest losses significantly. 

The program also aims to promote the use of modern technology in fisheries. 

By facilitating better transportation, the program encourages fishers to access larger markets. 

This can lead to better prices for their catch and increased profitability. 

The government has allocated a substantial budget for the implementation of this program. 

In the financial year 2021-2022, the budget allocation for the fisheries sector was INR 1,500 crore. 

This reflects the government's commitment to enhancing the fisheries sector's contribution to the economy. 

The program also includes training and capacity-building initiatives for fishers. 

Workshops and training sessions are conducted to educate fishers about modern fishing techniques. 

This includes information on sustainable practices and market access strategies. 

The Intensive Fisheries Development Programme is a vital component of India's rural development strategy. 

It aims to uplift the socio-economic status of fishers and their families. 

By providing financial assistance for transportation, the program directly impacts their livelihoods. 

The government continuously monitors the implementation of this program. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further. 

The success of the program is measured through various indicators such as increased fish production. 

The government also tracks the number of beneficiaries who have availed of the subsidy. 

Overall, the Intensive Fisheries Development Programme represents a significant step towards enhancing the fisheries sector in India. 

It addresses critical challenges faced by fishers and promotes sustainable practices. 

The program is expected to play a crucial role in achieving the government's vision for the fisheries sector. 

By focusing on transportation and operational efficiency, it aims to create a more robust fisheries economy. 

The subsidy on commercial four-wheeler vehicles is just one of the many initiatives under this program. 

The government remains committed to supporting the fisheries sector through various welfare schemes. 

This commitment is reflected in the continuous allocation of resources and support for fishers. 

The program is a testament to the government's efforts to improve the livelihoods of those in the fisheries sector. 

The Intensive Fisheries Development Programme is a comprehensive approach to fisheries development in India. 

It combines financial assistance with capacity building and sustainable practices. 

This holistic approach is essential for the long-term growth of the fisheries sector. 

The program is expected to have a lasting impact on the lives of fishers across the country. 

By enhancing their operational capabilities, the program contributes to food security and economic development.
